title: Bounded amplitude of open direct image on classical torsion sheaves
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $\Lambda$ be a finite ring with $\ell^r\Lambda=0$ for
some $r\ge1$, and let $j:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion of
finite-type $k$-schemes. Put $d=\operatorname{cd}(j)$ in the sense of
[def-kun-cd]. Then $d<\infty$, and:

1. for every sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ and every
   $q>d$, $R^qj_{\mathrm{ét},*}F=0$;
2. for every such $F$ and every $q>d$,
   $\mathcal H^q\bigl(Rj_{\mathrm{proét},*}\nu_X^*F\bigr)=0$, where
   $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proét}}\to X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ is the comparison morphism;
3. consequently, if $M\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{ét}},\Lambda)$ has cohomology in
   degrees $[a,b]$, then $Rj_{\mathrm{proét},*}\nu_X^*M$ has cohomology in
   degrees $[a,b+d]$.

proof.text: Geometric hypotheses and finiteness. The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$), so $X$ and $Y$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], every open subset of either scheme is quasi-compact. Hence any morphism with source $X$ or $Y$ is quasi-compact: the inverse image of an affine open is an open subset of its source. Apply the same observation to their diagonals and to the diagonal of $j$, whose sources are $X$ or $Y$, to obtain quasi-separatedness. Thus $X,Y$ and $j$ satisfy the qcqs hypotheses of [def-kun-cd]. The compatible $k$-structure maps on $X,Y$ make $j$ a morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes, so clause (1) of [lem-kun-0f10] gives $d=\operatorname{cd}(j)<\infty$. The convention in [def-kun-cd] then makes $d$ a nonnegative integer, including when $X$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 0F10, lemma-finite-cd (1); geometric hypotheses from Tags 01T6, 01OZ, 04ZA

proof.text: Resolution setup, without a commutativity restriction on $\Lambda$. Use left modules and the etale and pro-etale coefficient categories of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], in a common larger universe containing their small sites and all coefficient values. For either site and any ring sheaf, [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] gives a Grothendieck abelian module category. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-functorial-injective-embedding] and iterate embeddings of successive cokernels to obtain enough injectives, also for abelian sheaves by taking the integer ring sheaf. By [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative], a sheaf $F[0]$ admits an injective representative $I^\bullet$ with $I^m=0$ for $m<0$. The derived direct image is represented by $j_*I^\bullet$; this is precisely the K-injective computation in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Underived module direct image evaluates on $V\times_YX$ with the induced scalar action. It is additive and left exact because limits and kernels are computed on sections. Forgetting the action is exact and preserves kernels and cokernels by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. In particular it commutes with cohomology of complexes and reflects zero: a module sheaf with zero underlying abelian sheaf has only its zero section everywhere.

source.place: Tags 03DA, 03DB, 03EW (Grothendieck module categories); injectives.tex Tag 079H; derived.tex Tags 013K, 070J

proof.text: Compare module and abelian higher direct images. For each injective etale $\Lambda$-module sheaf $I$ and each object $U$ of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison] identifies $H^q(U,I_{ab})$ with the module-derived evaluation of $I$. It vanishes for $q>0$: an injective object is acyclic for any left exact additive functor by clause (1) of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity], applied to evaluation. For every etale $V\to Y$, take $U=X\times_YV$. The abelian higher direct image $R^qj_*I_{ab}$ is the sheafification of $V\mapsto H^q(X\times_YV,I_{ab})$ by [lem-weil-pbc-higher-direct-image-sheafified-presheaf]; hence $I_{ab}$ is $j_*$-acyclic. The resolution $F\to I^\bullet$ of step 2 remains an exact resolution after forgetting. Clause (2) of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity], now for abelian $j_*$, therefore computes $R^qj_*F_{ab}$ by $H^q(j_*I^\bullet_{ab})$. This is the underlying abelian sheaf of the module $R^qj_{\mathrm{et},*}F$, since forgetting is exact and commutes with underived direct image on sections. This proves the coefficient-forgetting comparison used here without asserting that forgetting preserves injectives. It also gives zero cohomology in degrees $q<0$, directly from $I^m=0$ for $m<0$.

source.place: Tag 03FD, lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree; Tag 072W, lemma-higher-direct-images; derived.tex Tag 015E, lemma-leray-acyclicity

proof.text: Etale sheaf bound, clause (1). Every local section of $F$ is killed by $\ell^r$, so $F_{ab}$ is torsion. Independently, finiteness of $\Lambda$ gives a positive additive exponent annihilating $1_\Lambda$ and hence every section of every left $\Lambda$-module; thus this assertion uses no invertibility condition on $k$. The definition [def-kun-cd] says that $R^qj_*F_{ab}=0$ for $q>d$. Step 3 identifies this with the underlying abelian sheaf of $R^qj_{\mathrm{et},*}F$. Forgetting reflects zero by step 2, proving (1).

source.place: Proof paragraph (1), after finiteness; Stacks 0F10 and the definition preceding lemma-finite-cd

proof.text:
Comparison and the pro-etale sheaf bound, clause (2). For every $L\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, the qcqs property from step 1 allows [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] to identify $Rj_{\mathrm{proet},*}
u_X^*L$ with $
u_Y^*Rj_{\mathrm{et},*}L$. Exactness of $
u_Y^*$ for finite $\Lambda$ is [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level]. Applying it to the kernel, image and cokernel that define cohomology gives, for every complex $C$, $\mathcal H^q(
u_Y^*C)\cong
u_Y^*\mathcal H^q(C)$; this calculation descends to the derived category since it also shows preservation of quasi-isomorphisms. Thus for $L=F[0]$,
$$\mathcal H^q(Rj_{\mathrm{proet},*}
u_X^*F)\cong
u_Y^*R^qj_{\mathrm{et},*}F.$$
It vanishes for $q>d$ by step 4 and for $q<0$ by step 3. This proves (2) and the full interval $[0,d]$ on classical sheaves.

source.place: Tag 09A6, lemma-morphism-comparison (2); blueprint proof paragraph (2), with exactness applied explicitly to cohomology

proof.text:
Bounded complexes, clause (3). Apply [thm-sp-truncation-e2] to the additive left exact functor $v=j_{\mathrm{et},*}$ between the Grothendieck module categories of step 2. A bounded-below representative exists by step 2. Its convergent truncation spectral sequence is
$$E_2^{p,q}=R^pj_{\mathrm{et},*}\mathcal H^q(M)\Longrightarrow\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rj_{\mathrm{et},*}M).$$
By step 4 and the hypothesis on $M$, its $E_2$ terms vanish unless $0\le p\le d$ and $a\le q\le b$. Hence for any total degree $n<a$ or $n>b+d$ all $E_2$ terms, and therefore all their later subquotients $E_\infty^{p,n-p}$, vanish. Clauses (5) and (6) of the cited theorem give a finite exhaustive separated filtration of $\mathcal H^n(Rj_{\mathrm{et},*}M)$ with precisely these associated graded objects. Successively using $F^p/F^{p+1}=0$ shows that all filtration terms equal one another, so the zero end term equals the whole object. Thus the abutment is zero in those degrees. This is the finite canonical-truncation argument in the blueprint's paragraph (3), expressed through its exact couple, including the zero complex and missing cohomology degrees. Finally use the comparison for $L=M$ and the cohomology calculation in step 5 to get
$$\mathcal H^n(Rj_{\mathrm{proet},*}\nu_X^*M)\cong\nu_Y^*\mathcal H^n(Rj_{\mathrm{et},*}M)=0$$
outside $[a,b+d]$. If $a>b$, all cohomology of $M$ is zero and the same finite-filtration argument gives zero in every degree. No constructibility, separatedness over $k$, or finite absolute cohomological dimension of $k$ is used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q73-404ad5b11 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, the report, the unit and chapter records, the blueprint statement and proof (main-20261015), and every cited statement in full. Also read Stacks at the cited places: 0F10 lemma-finite-cd (1), 03FD, 0D6J (3) and 09A6 (2). The item's statement matches the blueprint word for word, with nothing weakened. The coefficients are any finite associative ring Λ with left modules. The direct-image comparison is the canonical mate, and its Lean declaration takes [Ring Λ] [Finite Λ], so no commutative-only comparison has been swapped in. The commutative-only det-pbc-conventions-module-cohomology is correctly not cited. Step 1: k is Noetherian, so X, Y and j are qcqs and 0F10 (1) gives d<∞. Assertion (2), which needs a hypothesis on k, is not used. Steps 2-3: the Grothendieck property needs no commutativity; injective representatives give a resolution. The 03FD evaluation comparison, Leray acyclicity and the sheafified higher-direct-image formula then prove 0D6J (3) on D^+, without claiming that forgetting preserves injectives. Step 4: F is torsion, def-kun-cd gives the vanishing, and forgetting reflects zero. Step 5: the qcqs comparison together with exactness of ν^* for finite Λ gives the interval [0,d]. Step 6: the hypotheses of thm-sp-truncation-e2 hold. The E_2 terms lie in the rectangle 0≤p≤d, a≤q≤b, and the finite filtration of clauses 5-6 gives [a,b+d]; this agrees with the blueprint's truncation induction. Tested cases: a sheaf in degree m gives [m,m+d]; j=id gives d=0; empty X, Λ=0, a>b; char k=ℓ; noncommutative Λ. There are no new nodes. The duplicate search over 0D6J/072W/03FD, open-finiteness and cd(j) found only nodes with stronger hypotheses. There are no cycles and no restated clauses.
